## Design

### 2026-10-11 – Making the schematic was pretty straightforward, but laying out the pcb took me a while because I had to learn about where to place mounting screws on a pcb, and not to leave empty vias everywhere. I

**4h**

Making the schematic was pretty straightforward, but laying out the pcb took me a while because I had to learn about where to place mounting screws on a pcb, and not to leave empty vias everywhere. I also improved the efficiency of my pcb trace routing, in previous projects I’ve done, I have been more focused on just getting everything connected than on making it compact and reusing sections of copper tracing whenever possible. I also decided to add a place on my pcb where I could attach a plantower pms5003 I used in a previous project that was just built around the sensor and an arduino uno on a breadboard. Next session I’ll work on the software/firmware components.
ps. I forgot to take photos along the way so here are photos of my pcb layout, my schematic layout, and my breadboard project that inspired me to add the pms5003 to this project(more so the remains of it, it was sitting in my parts bin for a while.)
pps. I know it’s a bit unrelated, but I also attached a photo of the m6600 I just finished repairing that I’ll hopefully use for kicad in the future (as soon as I can find a proper 240w charger for it instead of the 130w one I’m using now that gives an unusable framerate in kicad because of how much the cpu gets throttled.(the problem with the laptop I used for this project, is it is a school device and as such I can’t record the screen for timelapses, so images are all for now.)
